note: Independent re-judgment after 381e927417 against RFC 6396 Section 4.2 ("The TABLE_DUMP Type does not permit 4-byte Peer AS numbers, nor does it allow the AFI of the peer IP to differ from the AFI of the Prefix field.  The TABLE_DUMP_V2 Type MUST be used in these situations."). writeTableDumpV2 now sends both visitor callbacks through one writeRoute closure whose writeHeader stamps mrtfmt.TypeTableDumpV2 for every subtype it can pick (2-5, 6, 8-12); writePeerIndexTable stamps TypeTableDumpV2, and every OnPeer entry is PeerAS4 (plus PeerIPv6 for an IPv6 peer). No writer in internal/plugins/mrt or internal/mrt emits TypeTableDump (12): it appears only in types.go and the reader. TestDumpV2PeerWidthAndPrefixFamily (unchanged) drives writeTableDumpV2 over all eight IPv4/IPv6 peer x IPv4/IPv6 prefix x 2-/4-octet ASN combinations and fails on the first header that is not TABLE_DUMP_V2, then pins the PIT peer type, 4-octet ASN, address and BGP ID and the RIB prefix, peer index and attributes. It drives OnRoute only; OnRouteAddPath shares the same closure and type constant. TestRibSubtype is supplementary (subtype mapping only, not the Type). Stale prose, not a verdict change: TestRibSubtype's comment cites dump.go:206-219, :171,200 and :133-135, and the {single-polarity} annotation cites dump.go:113 and :206; none of those lines holds what it names any more. The annotation's argument still holds: no Ze path emits TABLE_DUMP, so there is no violating output to refuse.
